questions.q: Why did configure_azure_monitor() and the KQL query in Lesson 29 feel like reaching for a known tool rather than learning something new mid-lab?
options: Because Lesson 29 included a full Azure Monitor tutorial from scratch
Because Chapter 2's Azure Monitor deep dive had already covered Log Analytics and Application Insights before this capstone needed them
Because Azure Monitor requires no prior knowledge to use
Because KQL is identical to Python syntax
questions.explain: Chapter 2 already built the Azure Monitor vocabulary -- Log Analytics, Application Insights, KQL -- so the capstone could use those tools directly instead of introducing them.

questions.q: Why did Lesson 30 pin the cost view onto the same dashboard as Chapter 4's Grafana panels, instead of building it as a separate chart?
options: Grafana cannot display cost data under any circumstances
Pinning charts together is required by Azure
On the explicit principle, from Chapter 4, that a dashboard should answer a real question rather than just display an isolated metric
Because Cost Management doesn't support chart pinning
questions.explain: Chapter 4 taught designing dashboards around real questions, not vanity metrics -- the reason cost and reliability views were deliberately placed side by side rather than kept separate.

questions.q: What role did Chapter 6's right-sizing discipline play in setting up Lesson 31's incident?
options: It correctly flagged the node pool as over-provisioned at 52% average utilization -- a valid cost signal on its own, but one that still needed a reliability reviewer before becoming a merged change
It had no connection to the incident at all
It was responsible for causing the traffic spike
It directly caused the autoscaler to fail
questions.explain: The right-sizing signal itself was correct and legitimate -- Chapter 6 working as intended. What was missing was a reliability reviewer connecting that signal to the SLO's headroom dependency.

questions.q: What specifically from Chapter 7 turned 'latency went up for four minutes' into a measurable incident severity in Lesson 31?
options: The cost dashboard from Lesson 30
The structured logging formatter from Lesson 29
The az resource tag command
SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets, which quantified the event as 19 of 43 error-budget minutes consumed, and the blameless postmortem process that produced process fixes rather than blame
questions.explain: Chapter 7's error-budget concept gave the incident a quantified severity, and its blameless postmortem format shaped the root-cause analysis and corrective actions.

questions.q: According to this review lesson, what is the actual point of the whole chapter 8 capstone, beyond the four individual lessons?
options: That cost optimization should always be avoided
That observability, dashboards, and FinOps are one operating practice, and reviewing any one of them in isolation from the others is what makes an incident like Lesson 31's possible
That SRE teams should have sole authority over all infrastructure changes
That Terraform and Kubernetes skills are no longer relevant
questions.explain: The capstone's real lesson is integration: observability, cost management, and reliability engineering have to be reviewed together, not as three separate, isolated disciplines.
